entry.title: Wits and UJ researchers show early-warning systems for disengaged students are often tested unfairly
entry.summary:
Researchers from University of the Witwatersrand and University of Johannesburg, for one early paper wey dem never review yet, show say early-warning system wey dey find students wey dey disengage from study dey often test with information wey no go dey available for real as dem dey make di prediction, and dis one dey make di system look better pass how e go be for real use. As dem test three prediction methods on 49,329 weekly, real-time predictions wey come from Moodle learning system records, dem find out say no single method win for every measure, and say if dem lower di alert level, e go catch more students wey dey risk but e go also increase false alarm wey staff go need handle.

Why e matter for AHEAD: This one important for Wits AHEAD Pillar 2 work on predictive analytics for student success because e give South African universities one more honest way to check, before dem go depend on am, if early-warning system go really help catch students wey dey disengage on time, no be just how e dey look after everything don happen.

arXiv (preprint) · Preprint (not yet peer-reviewed)

entry.title: Generative AI access does not mean equal use, study of Chinese, Japanese and Mongolian students finds
entry.summary:
One study wey compare 42 undergraduate students, one university each for China, Japan and Mongolia, find out say just to get access to generative AI no mean say e go useful for study for everybody the same way. Researchers from University of Osaka, University of Minnesota, Waseda University and Kyoto University talk say China students dey switch between local and global AI tools, Japan students dey mostly use global tools for Japanese language, while Mongolia students dey often switch go English when the answer for Mongolian language look weak; all three groups dey also check accuracy, privacy, how much dem dey depend on am, and how e dey affect dia own thinking before dem go trust an answer.

Why e matter for AHEAD: This one na warning for Wits AHEAD Pillar 1 work on generative AI for higher education: language and local technical condition, no be access alone, na im dey decide if generative AI dey really help students learn, lesson wey apply directly to university systems wey get plenty language, wey no be English be di main one, across the Global South.

arXiv (preprint) · Preprint (not yet peer-reviewed)

entry.title: Kyoto University framework offers universities a safer way to share student data with researchers
entry.summary:
Researchers from Kyoto University propose ReLEAF, one framework wey go make universities and online learning platforms fit share di learning data wey dem collect with outside researchers, while dem dey protect student privacy well well. E first give researchers safe fake data wey dem fit use explore, before dem go give controlled access to real data only after dem agree one specific research need with di institution wey hold di data. Dem design and test dis one through plenty rounds of work with data custodians, researchers and students for Japan universities.

Why e matter for AHEAD: This one important for Wits AHEAD Pillar 5 work on analytics and data for education systems because plenty universities, including for Global South, get rich student data but dem no get safe process wey everybody agree to share am with researchers; dis one give practical example wey institutions fit adapt.

arXiv (preprint) · Preprint (not yet peer-reviewed)

entry.title: UNESCO opens global consultation on governing AI so that education remains a common good
entry.summary:
UNESCO don open one global discussion wey go run reach November 2026, dem dey invite academics and policy people make dem comment on some background papers wey dey talk about how to govern AI inside education. Di main paper, wey dem release before Digital Learning Week 2026, show six ways wey education purpose fit spoil if dem no govern how AI dey used, and e talk say education suppose remain something wey belong to everybody, instead of leave di governing to AI companies.

Why e matter for AHEAD: Dis discussion go shape how UNESCO go guide ministries and universities for future, dis na why e important for Wits AHEAD pillar wey dey cover responsible AI, ethics, equity and policy, especially for institutions for Global South wey no get plenty capacity to write dia own AI governance framework.

UNESCO · Intergovernmental body, consultation paper

entry.title: Simple digital markers could flag at-risk first-year computer science students by week five, Southern African study finds
entry.summary:
Wen researchers check four batch of year-one computer science students for one big public university for sub-Saharan Africa, dem see say if you combine one score wey show how student dey push for im studies, with simple background info and just weda di student don log in to di course online learning system before, e fit correctly show 87 percent of students wey go later fail. Di researchers talk say di model simple well well, so dem fit use am as early-warning system from week five of term.

Why e matter for AHEAD: Dis kind simple, low-data early-warning tool fit universities wey no get plenty data infrastructure, and e dey push forward Wits AHEAD pillar for AI and predictive analytics for student success for places wey no get plenty resources.

arXiv (preprint) · Preprint (not yet peer-reviewed)

entry.title: Nigerian study finds male pre-service STEM teachers report higher AI literacy than female peers
entry.summary:
One study wey dem do for 541 students wey dey train to become STEM teachers for Lagos State University, wey dem publish inside STEM Education journal, show say di students rate dia sef AI knowledge well well, and say how dem understand AI fit tell weda dem go use am well for teaching. Di study also see one gender gap wey show clear well: male trainee teachers rate dia AI knowledge pass dia female colleagues.

Why e matter for AHEAD: Dis gap dey important for teacher-training programmes across di Global South, wey want make AI knowledge spread equal for di next generation of STEM teachers, na wetin Wits AHEAD dey focus on for di pillar wey dey cover AI and analytics for STEM and teacher education.

STEM Education (AIMS Press) · Peer-reviewed journal article

entry.title: Universities in Korea, Singapore and the United Kingdom take different paths to redesign teaching for AI

category.term: Korea, Singapore and the United Kingdom

entry.summary:
The Korea Times report say Korean universities don add more than 4,000 slots for AI and semiconductor related courses since 2024, and say application to AI departments for twenty big universities rise by 16% dis year, as government don cap new advanced technology slots to 434 for 2027 because dem no get enough staff and facilities. Di same report compare dis expansion to Nanyang Technological University for Singapore, wey dey plan to put AI inside 40% of dia degree courses by 2030, and to King's College London and London School of Economics, wey dey redesign how dem dey assess students and dey give students and staff license to use AI tools instead of go back to hand written exams.

Why e matter for AHEAD: For Wits AHEAD pillar wey dey focus on generative AI for higher education, dis comparison show two different way to handle di same pressure, to build more AI capacity or to redesign wetin and how dem dey assess students, one choice wey South African universities sef dey weigh for di same time.

The Korea Times · Established national press, first instalment of a three-part series

entry.title: Study proposes voice-based AI interviews as a richer alternative to end-of-semester course surveys
entry.summary:
Researchers from Technical University of Munich and MIT Sloan School of Management dey propose say make dem replace written end of semester course survey wit structured interview wey one voice AI agent go conduct, wey fit ask follow up questions wia written form no fit ask. One technical pilot for Technical University of Munich show say phone based AI interview dey possible, and di researchers dey plan now one full field study for one MIT Sloan course wit about 60 students, dem go score di feedback based on how specific, how rich di theme be, how constructive di tone be, and how deep di context be.

Why e matter for AHEAD: For Wits AHEAD pillar wey dey focus on generative AI for higher education, dis study show one practical way to use conversational AI inside teaching: to turn weak feedback wey few people dey respond to into one wey detailed well well, wey lecturers and institutions fit use take action.

Technical University of Munich and the MIT Sloan School of Management, posted to arXiv · Preprint (not yet peer-reviewed)

entry.title: Eduvos academic leader tells CNBC Africa that equal access to AI, not only AI literacy, will decide graduate employability
entry.summary:
For one AI summit wey CNBC Africa organize, one academic leader from Eduvos, private higher institution, talk say South African universities no fit wait again to decide wetin artificial intelligence mean for teaching and students, and say AI literacy, wey mean say you know wen to lean on AI and wen to think for yourself, dey important now like basic academic skills. Di leader warn say access to AI no be only access to degree: if students from poor background no get device, digital support and infrastructure, AI fit increase inequality instead to reduce am among graduates wey dey enter job market.

Why e matter for AHEAD: For Wits AHEAD pillar wey dey focus on graduate capability, employability and just transitions, dis interview dey remind us say how ready South African higher education be for AI depend well well on equal access to tools and infrastructure, just as e depend on teaching AI skills.

CNBC Africa · Broadcast interview, major African business channel

entry.title: Seven-country study finds universities at very different stages of AI readiness
entry.summary:
One study wey dem do for seven kontris by WISE and Institute of International Education find out say universities dey different stages well well for how dem ready for generative AI, as policy, student attitude and infrastructure no balance. For one private university for Ghana, 64 percent of lecturers talk say dem get clear AI policy, against 27 percent for one public research university, even though 89 percent of lecturers wey dem survey don already use AI demsef before. Di researchers warn say, because big AI models dey learn mainly from English and oda languages wey strong, African and oda Global South institutions fit remain pipo wey just dey use AI, instead of pipo wey dey build am.

Why e matter for AHEAD: For Wits AHEAD pillar wey dey focus on responsible AI, ethics, equity and policy, di study show say di gap for readiness between institutions, no be only between kontris, fit make inequality grow pass how e dey reduce am for how higher education dey adopt AI.

WISE and the Institute of International Education (IIE), reported by University World News · Established higher education press, reporting a WISE/IIE policy brief

entry.title: Dutch minister calls AI-written theses 'fraud', universities say detection scores cannot prove it
entry.summary:
One Dutch TV station check hundreds of recent master thesis for twelve universities and find out say for almost one out of five, chatbots like ChatGPT, Claude or Gemini write pass wetin di student write. Education minister, Rianne Letschert, call dis one fraud, but di body wey represent Dutch universities, Universiteiten van Nederland, talk say detection score alone no fit prove say person cheat, and say di real question na how dem design di assessment. Delft, Utrecht and Leiden don restrict or ban AI detection tools for student work, dem talk say di tools no dey reliable.

Why e matter for AHEAD: For Wits AHEAD pillar wey dey focus on generative AI for higher education, dis matter show how academic integrity wahala fit turn political sharp sharp once minister enter, and why di group dey push for make dem redesign assessment instead of depend on detection software.

Times Higher Education · Established higher education press

entry.title: Russell Group students say they are taught little about AI, Bett UK survey finds
entry.summary:
One Bett UK survey wey dem do for more than 1,000 UK undergraduate students find out say 77 percent of students for Russell Group universities talk say dem no dey teach dem much or nothing about AI, against 64 percent for post-1992 universities. Di same survey find out say 78 percent of students go like one degree wey technology personalize and wey go take shorter time, but na only 34 percent feel say dia university dey straight with dem about real work prospects after graduation. Russell Group talk say dia members dey redesign curriculum and assessment rules because of dis.

Why e matter for AHEAD: For Wits AHEAD pillar wey dey focus on generative AI for higher education, di finding say research heavy universities no teach AI skills well well like oda institutions dey raise straight equity question: which kain graduates go enter job market wey AI don change well prepared.

Times Higher Education · Established higher education press

entry.title: New framework guides statistics and data science educators on teaching responsible generative AI use
entry.summary:
Team of statistics and data science teachers release one framework wey get four parts, understanding, development, reporting and safety, to guide how lecturers go teach students to use generative AI tool well well for coding and statistics work. Dem don improve am through workshop and feedback from students, and dem don already use am for one free online course and for undergraduate and postgraduate teaching.

Why e matter for AHEAD: Pillar 3, AI and analytics for STEM and teacher education, need framework wey ready for classroom, no be policy statement alone; dis one give Wits AHEAD one working model to teach generative AI literacy inside number-based subject.

arXiv · Preprint (not yet peer-reviewed)

entry.title: New tool scrambles assignment images so AI reading systems fail, but people can still read them
entry.summary:
Some researchers build AIRRI, one tool wey dey change how image of printed assignment dey look, dem dey use spacing, opacity and noise plus adversarial attacks, so that OCR tools and AI chatbot go hard to read di work well well, but human eye fit still read am well. Dem test am against three reading system, and di strongest attack push one system error rate from 2.3% go 100%, and anoda one word error rate from 24.9% go 96.7%. Di team also release dataset of higher education assignment to test di method.

Why e matter for AHEAD: Pillar 1, na generative AI for higher education: teaching, assessment, integrity, need protection wey dey work for di assignment level itself; Wits AHEAD dey watch tool like dis to see if integrity fit dey build inside course material instead of dem go dey chase am afta di fact.

arXiv · Preprint (not yet peer-reviewed)

entry.title: New framework argues the cost of AI essay-marking systems should be measured against trustworthy scores, not efficiency alone
entry.summary:
New paper propose “Cost-Aware Measurement Design” framework for automated essay-scoring systems, e argue say di computing cost of AI marking na wetin pipo dey normally treat as simple technical efficiency matter, but e be measurement-design choice for real. Di framework define “cost per defensible score” wey dey compare scoring systems only among designs wey meet minimum standard of trustworthy measurement, e dey treat institution governance and oversight capacity as limit on which design dem fit use, no be price wey dem go reduce.

Why e matter for AHEAD: For Wits AHEAD pillar on generative AI for higher education, teaching, assessment and integrity, dis framework give universities wey dey consider AI-assisted marking one concrete way to ask whether cheaper system dey really produce score wey dem fit defend, instead of dem to judge automated assessment tools only by speed and cost.

arXiv (preprint) · Preprint (not yet peer-reviewed)

entry.title: Study of a South African university finds online “participation profiles” mostly track how long a learner is observed, not how engaged they are
entry.summary:
Afta dem analyse 16,448 student-course records from 4,599 students for 152 courses for one South African public university, researchers test eight measures wey pipo dey normally use for online “participation”, dem see say all of dem dey show how long dem observe student for course pass how di student really dey participate. Afta dem adjust dis one, small set of measures still dey group students into one broad two-profile pattern and one more detailed four-profile pattern, but di confidence no too strong.

Why e matter for AHEAD: For Wits AHEAD pillar on AI and predictive analytics for student success, dis finding be direct warning for early-warning and retention systems wey dem build with South African data: unless dem account for how long dem dey track student, profile wey dem mark as “no dey participate” fit just be student wey dem observe for short time, no be person wey really dey for risk.

arXiv (preprint) · Preprint (not yet peer-reviewed)

entry.title: Study finds students who earn the same grade can have done very different amounts of their own thinking with AI help
entry.summary:
Afta dem analyse 150 recorded conversation between students and generative AI tools, new study see say students wey direct di AI, wey dey critically integrate wetin e bring out, and wey dey carefully evaluate am fit get di same grade as students wey allow AI do most of di thinking for dem, so di final mark alone no dey show how much of di work na di student own real sense. Di author call dis gap “epistemic ownership” and argue say to grade only di output fit reward very different level of student involvement wit di same score.

Why e matter for AHEAD: For Wits AHEAD pillar on generative AI for higher education, teaching, assessment and integrity, dis study strengthen di argument for assessment wey go also check how student use AI during di task, no be only di finished product, becos two grade wey be di same fit hide very different learning.

arXiv (preprint) · Preprint (not yet peer-reviewed)

entry.title: Wits tells top applicants AI should make graduates indispensable, not just employable
entry.summary:
More than 200 top students wey pass well for matric, from Gauteng and oda places, attend di Wits Vice Chancellor Top Applicants Event, where Wits old student, Dr Craig Wing, give di main speech on top artificial intelligence and di future of work. Deputy Vice Chancellor, Professor Garth Stevens, tell di students say university na responsibility, no be just road to job, and say Wits want im graduates to pass employable, e want dem to be indispensable.

Why e matter for AHEAD: For Wits AHEAD pillar on top AI, graduate capability, employability and just transition, dis event show say di University dey prepare new students for job market wey AI done change, from di first day dem enter Wits, instead of leave employability matter for after graduation.

Wits University · University announcement

entry.title: Study finds AI grading tools miss most student misconceptions despite accurate scores
entry.summary:
New study check whether di big AI language models wey dey grade open-ended assignment for higher education dey useful well well like how dia accuracy score show. Afta dem analyse 3,041 student answers to 50 open-ended computer science questions, wey human teachers and three commercial AI language models grade, di researchers see say AI-generated feedback only catch student misconceptions for 5 to 7 per cent of di cases, compared to 15 to 31 per cent for human teachers, and di AI feedback stay positive-positive no matter how di answer quality be. Di study also see say AI-generated rubric sub-scores dey match well well wit demsef, so dem no give much independent diagnostic information.

Why e matter for AHEAD: For Wits AHEAD pillar on generative AI for higher education, teaching, assessment and integrity, di finding say AI grading fit look correct but still miss most of di reasoning errors wey matter for teaching, be warning say make pipo no use automated marking replace teacher diagnostic judgement.

arXiv (preprint) · Preprint (not yet peer-reviewed)

entry.title: California requires its public colleges to set AI procurement and training standards
entry.summary:
California don sign Assembly Bill 2392 (AB 2392) into law, and e dey mandate di California Community Colleges and California State University systems to come together form one working group wey go recommend standards for how to buy and train staff and students on generative AI systems, and dem suppose bring di recommendations before January 2028. Dem chaptered di law on 30 September 2026 as Chapter 855 of di Statutes of 2026, and e also mandate both systems to dey review AI training at least once every year, and to report to di state legislature within 60 days after dem sign any systemwide generative AI contract.

Why e matter for AHEAD: For Wits AHEAD pillar wey dey focus on responsible AI, ethics, equity and policy, di way California put public procurement and training standards inside law, instead of make dem leave generative AI wahala for individual schools, na Global North example of how dem fit govern AI for whole system level, and na di kain thing wey dem dey push Global South higher education systems make dem build too.

California State Legislature · State legislation

entry.title: University of Johannesburg vice-chancellor: Africa needs AI governance beyond regulation
entry.summary:
For one informal interview wit CNBC Africa, di vice-chancellor of University of Johannesburg, Professor Letlhokwa Mpedi, yarn wit di channel editor-in-chief, Godfrey Mutizwa, about wetin e go take to govern artificial intelligence (AI) for Africa pass just to regulate am. Di conversation touch di role wey universities and policy makers suppose play to shape how AI go develop for di continent, instead of just to dey react to rules wey dem make for odda places.

Why e matter for AHEAD: For Wits AHEAD pillar wey dey focus on responsible AI, ethics, equity and policy, one sitting South African vice-chancellor wey dey push for Africa-led AI governance dey talk directly to Wits AHEAD mission to build African capability to set di terms of AI development, no just to comply wit framework wey dem design for odda places.

CNBC Africa · Broadcast interview, major African business channel

entry.title: Joining up AI across recruitment, retention and alumni relations can close graduation gaps, if it is governed well
entry.summary:
Writing for University World News, IREX project director Cameron Mirza argue say universities suppose treat recruitment, retention and alumni relations as one connected, AI supported lifecycle instead of separate systems wey get separate data. E cite Georgia State University chatbot and predictive analytics programme, wey dem credit say e don cut "summer melt" by about 21 percent and don help Black, Hispanic, first generation and low income students graduate for rates wey match or pass di wider student body, but e warn say models wey dem train with historical data fit still entrench di inequities wey dem suppose fix.

Why e matter for AHEAD: For Wits AHEAD pillar on AI and predictive analytics for student success, dis piece na good reminder say early-warning and retention tools go only close equity gap if dem pair am with human oversight and bias testing, na di same governance question Wits AHEAD dey ask for any analytics tool wey e recommend.

University World News · Established higher education press (commentary by a sector practitioner)

entry.title: Wits researchers argue Africa must set its own AI research agenda, not just apply others' tools
entry.summary:
Two computer scientists for University of di Witwatersrand, Benjamin Rosman and Steve James, wey dey co-direct di Robotics, Autonomous Intelligence and Learning (RAIL) Lab, dey argue say Africa suppose drive artificial intelligence research instead of just dey use tools wey dem build for oda places. Dem point to Deep Learning Indaba, wey don become di world biggest AI summer school, wey bring 1,300 participants go last year gathering for Kigali, and wey dey run im IndabaX programme for 48 out of Africa 54 kontris dis year, plus Wits new Machine Intelligence and Neural Discovery (MIND) Institute, wey bring togeda around 65 academics across computer science, neuroscience, psychology and policy.

Why e matter for AHEAD: For Wits AHEAD pillar on responsible AI, ethics, equity and policy, di warning against Africa becoming just "a place where oda people dey do science" dey speak straight to Wits AHEAD own mission to build African led capability to set AI research questions, no be just to use AI tools wey dem design for oda places.

Times Higher Education · Established higher education press

entry.title: Study of students in China, Japan and Mongolia finds access to generative AI does not guarantee it is useful for learning
entry.summary:
One working paper wey study 42 undergraduates for one university each for China, Japan and Mongolia find out say how students dey reach generative AI, directly, through global platforms, or by switching language, dey shape whether e dey really useful for dem, no be just weda dem fit access am. Mongolian students, for example, often switch to English when Mongolian language outputs no reach standard, while all three groups weigh accuracy, privacy, dependence and how di tool dey affect dia own critical thinking. Di authors, Ming Li, Qin Xie, Ariunaa Enkhtur, Lilan Chen and Fei Cheng, conclude say technological access alone no guarantee equal educational use across different language and technology settings.

Why e matter for AHEAD: For Wits AHEAD pillar on generative AI for higher education, di finding say language and local technology conditions, no be connectivity alone, dey decide whether generative AI truly dey help students learn na warning Wits AHEAD dey apply di same way to English-dominant AI tools wey dem dey use across multilingual Southern African campuses.

arXiv (working paper) · Working paper (preprint, not yet peer-reviewed)

entry.title: South African minister tells universities to move from AI debate to decisions on teaching and research
entry.summary:
For di 4th Universities South Africa Higher Education Conference wey hold on 7 October 2026, South Africa Minister of Higher Education and Training, Buti Manamela, tell universities say artificial intelligence dey make dia main work, wey be to teach critical thinking and make people take responsibility for knowledge, important well well, no be less important, bikos AI systems fit produce confident content without check if e dey true. E add say di real question no be only wetin students dey use AI do for assignment, na who build di technology, whose language and experience e dey show, who dey control di infrastructure and who dey benefit, and e call for humanities and social sciences to work togeda wit engineering and natural sciences on di bias, power and labour wahala wey AI fit bring.

Why e matter for AHEAD: For Wits AHEAD pillar on generative AI for higher education, as one cabinet minister come dey lay out clear agenda for teaching, assessment and research capacity instead of just general argument, e dey give South African universities clear mandate to act on.

South African Government News Agency (SAnews) · National government news agency

entry.title: UNESCO study finds 87% of Latin American and Caribbean universities already use AI, but only 26% have a formal strategy
entry.summary:
One UNESCO IESALC working paper wit UNU-IAS, wey survey 200 higher education institutions across 19 Latin American and Caribbean kontris between August and October 2025, find out say 87 percent don already dey use AI for at least one area, lead by teaching and learning (74 percent) and research (57 percent), but only 26 percent get formal AI strategy and 55 percent no get dedicated AI budget at all. Adoption and governance dey follow institutional type well well: 84 percent of private non-profit universities dey use AI against 68 percent of public universities, and 17 percent of public universities report say dem no get staff training at all, against 3 percent of private non-profit ones.

Why e matter for AHEAD: For Wits AHEAD pillar on responsible AI, ethics, equity and policy, di finding say AI use don already spread wide while formal governance dey lag far behind, and e no balance across public and private institutions, dey mirror di governance gap Wits AHEAD dey see across di wider Global South.

UNESCO IESALC and UNU-IAS, reported by Times Higher Education · Established higher education press, reporting a UNESCO/UNU-IAS working paper

entry.title: UTeach survey finds STEM teacher-training staff cautiously optimistic about AI but wary of integrity and bias risks
entry.summary:
One survey of 57 faculty, administrators and staff from 31 university-based secondary STEM teacher-training programmes across 54 colleges and universities for United States find out say 77 percent agree say AI fit affect dia work well well, and 61 percent call demsef proactive adopters. 63 percent still worry about challenges, mostly academic integrity (42 percent) and ethical bias (21 percent), and 70 percent talk say dem need more training; 79 percent of instructors already dey use AI for dia courses, mostly for lesson planning and assessment design instead of data-heavy STEM inquiry.

Why e matter for AHEAD: For Wits AHEAD pillar on AI and analytics for STEM and teacher education, di gap between faculty wey don already dey try AI and di shared, research-based framework wey dem talk say dem no get, na exactly di kain structured guidance teacher-training programmes across Global South go also need.

The UTeach Institute, The University of Texas at Austin · University research institute report

entry.title: Systematic review finds no existing framework yet addresses the ethical and instructional challenges of AI in STEM teaching
entry.summary:
One systematic review by researchers for Wentworth Institute of Technology and di University of New Haven check established frameworks like TPACK, SAMR, ADDIE and Universal Design for Learning against AI literacy models and principles of responsible AI, to see how well dem fit support STEM instructors teaching practice. Dem find out say none of dis frameworks don address di professional, ethical and instructional challenges of using AI for STEM education, and say adoption of AI tools dey outpace systematic pedagogical guidance, wey make am tool-driven instead of framework-driven practice.

Why e matter for AHEAD: For Wits AHEAD pillar on AI and analytics for STEM and teacher education, di finding say no current instructional framework cover AI ethical and pedagogical wahala dey strengthen di case for di group own work on responsible, STEM-specific AI integration.

American Society for Engineering Education (ASEE), North East Section Conference · Peer-reviewed conference paper

entry.title: More universities end Turnitin contracts as concerns mount
entry.summary:
Times Higher Education report say Newcastle University and University of Westminster don join University of Southampton to end dia contract wit Turnitin, di plagiarism-detection company, afta Turnitin propose licence changes wey fit make dem use student coursework to train AI tools. Newcastle mention dat data clause direct; Westminster talk say Turnitin plagiarism checker 'largely ineffective' against AI-written text, and dia AI detector get 'a recognised risk of false positives'. Southampton alone pay Turnitin £87,621 for one year, out of student population wey pass 17,000 undergraduates and 8,000 postgraduates.

Why e matter for AHEAD: For Wits AHEAD pillar on responsible AI, ethics, equity and policy, dis matter show say universities dey start to weigh data governance and how reliable AI-detection tools really be against cost, instead of treating plagiarism-checking contract as something wey must dey fixed forever.

Times Higher Education · Established higher education press

entry.title: Prepare students for post-graduation AI judgement challenges
entry.summary:
University World News talk say di way higher education dey respond to generative AI dey stop too early, for graduation time, wen di real test of professional judgement go come afta. Dem cite one 2026 field experiment wey dem register beforehand, inside di journal Organization Science, wia 758 Boston Consulting Group consultants do real-life work wit or witout generative AI assistant: for most of di tasks, di ones wey use AI work faster and better, but for one task wey pass wetin di tool fit do, na only 70.6% of di AI-assisted consultants get di correct answer, against 84.5% for dose wey work witout AI, and di graders wey no know di answer rate di wrong AI-assisted recommendations as convincing as di correct ones.

Why e matter for AHEAD: For Wits AHEAD pillar on AI, graduate capability, employability and just transitions, dis finding wey show say confident but wrong AI-assisted work fit read as convincing as correct work dey point to professional judgement, no be AI literacy alone, as di capability wey graduates need well-well before dem enter di job market.

University World News · Established higher education press, commentary citing a peer-reviewed field experiment

entry.title: UNESCO and Codemao's AI coding drive reaches more African classrooms
entry.summary:
UNESCO and Chinese coding platform Codemao talk say di joint youth coding initiative dey continue to grow for Africa. Di second phase, wey go run reach 2030, don already train 200 teachers for Republic of Congo, Kenya, Namibia and Thailand, 45% of dem na women, and Kenya don get 200 tablets for 20 junior secondary schools.

Why e matter for AHEAD: For Wits AHEAD pillar on AI and analytics for STEM and teacher education, dis initiative show one way wey dem fit build AI and coding skill among teachers for Global South, wit special focus on women.

Xinhua (New China TV) · Major international news agency, video report

entry.title: PISA 2025 finds AI chatbot use split with student learning outcomes
entry.summary:
Di first PISA 2025 test from OECD wey check how students dey use AI, ask over 760,000 students wey dey 15 years old for 91 countries. Dem find out say students wey dey depend too much on AI chatbot to write dia assignment get lower science score, while students wey dey use AI small-small wit guidance show different and better pattern; reading and maths score sef don drop well-well for OECD countries for di past ten years.

Why e matter for AHEAD: For Wits AHEAD pillar on AI wey dey generate content for higher education, teaching, assessment and integrity, dis one na early sign of di habit wey students go carry come university, and wetin university go need teach and assess.

OECD (via Newsweek) · Intergovernmental body's flagship international assessment, reported by established press

entry.title: Understanding ethical dimensions of AI in higher education: insights from faculty members and students
entry.summary:
One study wey mix different research methods ask 971 students and 135 lecturers, den interview 23 students and 14 lecturers, about AI ethics for higher education. Both groups agree generally say dem must use AI well-well, but dia views differ: lecturers talk say ethics matter well but dia schools no get clear guidelines, while students see AI as something wey dey help dem learn but dem no sure where dia own responsibility stop.

Why e matter for AHEAD: For Wits AHEAD pillar on AI wey get responsibility, ethics, equity and policy, di study recommendations, lecturer training, special ethics courses and clear university guidelines, give practical checklist for institutions wey never get formal AI ethics policy.

International Journal of Educational Technology in Higher Education · Peer-reviewed journal article

entry.title: From AI literacy to action: South Africa charts a path forward for teacher education
entry.summary:
South Africa Department of Higher Education and Training and Commonwealth of Learning hold one national workshop wey last two days on AI for teacher education, for University of Pretoria Future Africa campus. Teachers, policy people and system leaders agree on one flexible national policy wey dey based on principles, dem form one national task team, make di result feed into di ongoing review of di Minimum Requirements for Teacher Education Qualifications, wey di people wey dey attend talk say no dey mention AI at all now.

Why e matter for AHEAD: For Wits AHEAD pillar on AI and analytics for STEM and teacher education, dis one show clear process, wey government dey lead, wey turn AI literacy to national qualification policy for South Africa teacher education system.

Commonwealth of Learning · Intergovernmental organisation report on a national government workshop

entry.title: Supporting cost-effective AI adoption in education
entry.summary:
World Bank don publish one working paper, Costing AI Use in Education in Low- and Middle-Income Countries, wit one blog post wey explain how ministries of education suppose budget for AI. E recommend say make dem start wit tools wey go help teachers, like lesson planning and feedback, instead of to roll am out to all students one time, make dem compare AI cost wit di cost wey dem dey spend now to expand normal teaching, and make dem use devices and mobile networks wey already dey schools. World Bank estimate say to reach di sustainable development goal for education for Sub-Saharan Africa go need extra six point four billion US dollars every year for primary school teachers and thirty-eight point seven billion dollars every year for secondary school teachers by 2030.

Why e matter for AHEAD: For Wits AHEAD pillar on analytics and data wey dey help education systems and decision-making, dis report give ministries and institutions for Global South one clear framework wey show di cost, to help dem decide where AI spending for education go do di most good.

World Bank · Intergovernmental body blog, summarising a World Bank working paper

entry.title: Grappling with "homework scams", US universities shun AI detectors
entry.summary:
One AFP report wey eNCA carry explain how Yale, Cornell and University of Wisconsin-Madison dey discourage or ban dia staff from use AI detection software as evidence of cheating, after studies find out say di tools no dey reliable and dem dey often flag innocent pipo wrongly, including pipo wey no be native English speaker. One biology lecturer for Wisconsin-Madison, wey hide one instruction inside assignment, catch 60 out of 350 students wey dey use AI without normal check dey see dem, and e dey move go oral exam and video debate instead of essay; one survey from American Association of Colleges and Universities and Elon University find out say 95% of lecturers dey fear say students dey depend too much on AI.

Why e matter for AHEAD: Generative AI for higher education, especially assessment and academic integrity, na di first pillar of Wits AHEAD, and dis one wey big universities dey waka commot from AI detection software na direct, practical sign for how di group suppose advise on assessment redesign instead of detection as answer to AI misuse.

AFP (via eNCA) · Established press (wire service report)

entry.title: Global Employment Trends for Youth 2026: Back to the Future
entry.summary:
Di International Labour Organization report, Global Employment Trends for Youth 2026, find out say world youth unemployment rate rise reach 12.4% for 2025, dis one leave around 67 million young pipo wey dia age dey between 15 to 24 without work, while around one out of five young pipo, around 257 million, no dey work, no dey school, and no dey train. Di report estimate say 6.1% of work wey young pipo wey dia age dey between 15 to 29 dey do fit face big risk from AI dey take over dia task, mostly office and clerical work wey don already dey shrink for young workers, and e dey call for human centred way to govern AI and technology, alongside more support to decent work.

Why e matter for AHEAD: Graduate employability and just transitions, including how AI dey change entry level work, na di fourth pillar of Wits AHEAD, and dis one wey dis intergovernmental report find out, say office work, wey often be first step for graduate, dey face di most risk from AI, give di group one concrete, global benchmark for dia work on AI and graduate employability for Global South.

International Labour Organization · Intergovernmental body report

entry.title: Generative AI use and misuse call for assessment reform in higher education
entry.summary:
One peer-reviewed study for di journal Science survey over 95,000 students for 20 big public research university for United States, for di 2023-24 school year. Dem find out say 37% of students dey use generative AI at least once every month for assignment, and di authors estimate say around 9% use am to cheat, dis one dey rise reach 26% among pipo wey dey use am every day; how pipo dey use am and dey cheat dey different well well according to course of study. Di authors talk say make dem change how dem dey assess student according to each course, instead of blanket ban or detection system for di whole university.

Why e matter for AHEAD: Generative AI for higher education, especially assessment and academic integrity, na di first pillar of Wits AHEAD, and dis big study wey show say misuse dey different according to course, no be di same everywhere, give di group real evidence to design assessment change wey dey fit each course, instead of one blanket change.

Science · Peer-reviewed journal article

entry.title: UCT summit puts AI, inequality and future of universities in spotlight
entry.summary:
Di Times Higher Education World Academic Summit open for University of Cape Town on 30 September 2026, na di first time dis summit dey happen for Africa. Around 600 higher education leaders, academics and policy makers from more than 60 kontris come join; di Vice-Chancellor, Professor Mosa Moshabela, talk say di future of di university no fit just dey depend on one technology. Di Minister of Higher Education, Buti Manamela, talk say AI suppose make education dey reach more people, wit wide AI literacy and better access to technology. UCT don stop to dey use AI-detection software, dem build dia own framework for how students and staff go dey use generative AI.

Why e matter for AHEAD: Fair access to generative AI for higher education na di first out of Wits AHEAD six pillars, and when minister talk say AI literacy, no be detection software, na im go bring fair access, na exactly wetin dis group policy and teaching work dey work on.

TimesLIVE · Established press

entry.title: Global Index on Responsible AI: 2026 Report
entry.summary:
Di Global Index on Responsible AI 2026, wey Global Center on AI Governance publish and launch for Geneva for July 2026, check governance for 135 kontris, dem use more than 68,000 data points wey dem collect between November 2023 and September 2025. Dem see say 126 out of di 135 kontris get at least one government policy or initiative about responsible AI, but dis one no too dey turn to protection wey dem fit enforce; AI literacy be one of di indicator wey dey perform well, 71 kontris, 53%, report say dem get framework, but less kontris get independent oversight body or monitoring system.

Why e matter for AHEAD: Responsible AI, ethics, equity and policy na di sixth pillar of Wits AHEAD, and wetin dis index see, say AI literacy policy dey move pass di institution wey fit enforce am, na exactly di governance gap wey dis group policy work dey try close for higher education for Global South.

Global Center on AI Governance · Independent global governance research index
